# Types and data (TYP)

The types and data rules of nuinashco/conventions: first the ones only judgement checks, in full, then the ones a tool checks.

## Apply with judgement

### TYP-6 MUST

Family bases are ABCs: the registry checks subclassing, and items inherit `Config` and helpers. An injected
collaborator that only needs a shape (a clock, an HTTP client, an uploader) is typed as a `Protocol`, so fakes need no
inheritance.

*Why:* [Hynek, "Subclassing in Python Redux"](https://hynek.me/articles/python-subclassing-redux/).

*Check:* review.

### TYP-7 SHOULD

Use `Literal` for small closed sets of config values, and `StrEnum` when code iterates over the set or attaches
behaviour to it.

*Check:* review.

### TYP-8 SHOULD

Avoid `Any` outside JSON-shaped payloads and lazily imported third-party objects. Use `object` for "accepts anything".

*Check:* review.

### TYP-9 MUST

Dicts are for wire payloads only (JSON in, JSON out). A dict with a fixed set of known keys is a class.

*Check:* review.

## Checked by tools

Linters, hooks and the template report these; follow them as you write.

- **TYP-1** MUST: Every function signature in `src/` is annotated; test functions and fixtures may skip annotations. pyright in standard mode passes on `src/` and `tests/`, and strict mode passes on the `src/` of a library other repos import, such as nuikit. *Check:* ruff ANN on `src/`; `make typecheck`.
- **TYP-2** MUST: Use modern syntax: `X | None`, builtin generics, `collections.abc` for abstract containers, PEP 695 generics and `type` aliases. *Check:* ruff UP.
- **TYP-3** MUST: While `requires-python` is below 3.14, every module starts with `from __future__ import annotations`. From 3.14 on it is never used: [PEP 649](https://peps.python.org/pep-0649/) makes annotations lazy, and [PEP 749](https://peps.python.org/pep-0749/) schedules the import for deprecation. *Check:* ruff I002 with `required-imports`, set by the template only for Python below 3.14.
- **TYP-4** MUST: pydantic is only for data parsed from outside: configs, HTTP bodies, files. Every other class is an attrs class: `@frozen` for values, `@define` for stateful objects, family bases and items included. *Check:* `check-conventions` flags dataclasses and a hand-written `__init__`, unless a base of the class is imported from outside the project; review for pydantic inside the boundary.
- **TYP-5** MUST: Mind three attrs behaviours, each verified on attrs 26.1: `@define` builds a new class, so a registering decorator must be the outermost one ([FAM-2](https://github.com/nuinashco/nuikit/blob/main/docs/guide.md#fam-2-must)); `__init_subclass__` runs twice for slotted classes, so hooks in it must be idempotent; Slots stop attribute typos only when every base class is slotted, which is why family bases are attrs classes too. *Check:* `nuikit` registry tests.
